key_insight: Reliable grading of agentic data-analysis outputs requires separating true answer disagreement from grading artifacts using a multi-stage human-AI cascade.
engineering_relevance: For evaluation pipelines in AI agents, combining strict parsing, lenient LLM grading, and targeted human inspection can dramatically improve robustness without sacrificing precision.
method: Applied LAMBDA to 153 numerical QRData tasks from DSGym.
Built a three-layer grading cascade: regex match, LLM lenient grading, and snippet-based human review.
Tested iterative nudging and question re-injection to improve answer extraction and grading success.
evidence_signal: On 153 tasks, both automated graders reached 100% observed precision (0/70 false positives), and the lenient grader achieved 97% recall against human labels.
watch_item: Results are from a specific case study and grading behavior may not generalize across task types, datasets, or systems without similar output structure.
paper_title: Grading the Grader: Lessons from Evaluating an Agentic Data Analysis System
